brief: How I raised my consulting rate to $1,200/hour — 5 mindset shifts that made it possible.

slots.subtitle: How I raised my rate to $1,200 an hour by changing nothing but my own mind.

slots.body: I was billing four hundred dollars and drowning in scope creep. The market was not the constraint; my unwillingness to repel the wrong buyers was. I had mistaken activity for leverage.
Clients do not purchase your time; they purchase the future state you architect. When I began quoting the value of the outcome rather than the cost of the clock, everything changed.
Availability is not a virtue in high-stakes advisory. I reduced my client load by half and raised my threshold for engagement. The harder I became to access, the more I was trusted.

Every unprofitable engagement consumes the energy required to attract the exceptional one. I learned to say no without apology, treating my calendar as a portfolio of concentrated bets, not a volume play.

There is no external examination that bestows the twelve-hundred-dollar hour. I stopped waiting for permission and began delivering my counsel as if the rate had always been mine. The market followed.
Luxury is communicated through restraint, not noise. I stripped my proposals of excess justification and let brevity imply mastery. When you stop explaining, you start commanding.
Your rate is a statement of how seriously you take your own expertise. Start there, and the right clients will already be waiting.
